target_customer: Engineering and security teams that pay for secrets, certificate and privileged access management
problem: Teams leak and sprawl API keys and credentials across code, CI and clouds. Infisical stores secrets and injects them into workflows, with rotation, audit and access controls.
business_model: Open core: MIT-licensed core, paid cloud and enterprise features

founders.name: Vlad Matsiiako
education: Cornell University, computer and data science
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (July 2023) says the three cofounders met at Cornell and worked at AWS, Figma and Bung, without assigning employers to individuals; recorded here as the group background.

founders.name: Tony Dang
education: Cornell University, computer and data science
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch spells the name Tuan Dang. Employer list is the group background, not individually attributed.

founders.name: Maidul Islam
education: Cornell University, computer and data science
founders.background_notes: Employer list is the group background, not individually attributed.

competitors.name: HashiCorp Vault
competitors.what: Open source secrets manager and enterprise product

technical_complexity.rationale: Secrets storage needs encryption, access control, audit and integrations with many clouds and CI systems. This is serious but well understood engineering; the founders started it as a side project at Cornell per YC video summary.

defensibility.rationale: Secrets managers sit deep in deployment pipelines, so customers rarely move, but Vault, cloud native tools and 1Password already exist and an open source core is forkable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents kept offering competing secrets tools through 2023 per TechCrunch and later comparison pages, yet Infisical kept raising and announced a $600M valuation in October 2026.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in July 2023 framed secret sprawl as a growing problem and named Vault, Doppler and Akeyless as existing tools, showing active spend. Vault's source-available license change is cited in later comparisons as a reason to look at open source options.

branding.domain_note: Uses infisical.com per the company website.

identity.voice_and_tone: Developer and security focused, open source

branding.brand_signature: Open source secrets manager with a large GitHub following
branding.community_and_virality: The about page lists over 30,000 GitHub stars and the README links a Slack community.

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive but hard to spell name; the open source repository and community drive awareness, but sources do not credit the name itself.

outcome_analysis: Infisical grew from a Cornell side project into a 70 person company by raising a $2.8M seed in July 2023, a $16M Series A in June 2025 and a $40M Series B at a reported $600M valuation in October 2026, all with Elad Gil involved. Open source distribution, a crowded but active market and the AI agent security theme drove growth. No layoffs, sale or incident was found.
notes: TechCrunch says Infisical raised $500K earlier through YC; this is the standard YC deal and is not a round. Sources disagree on the total raised (about $59M in SecurityWeek versus about $18.9M on Clay); neither is recorded. TechCrunch names the third cofounder Tuan Dang while the YC page says Tony Dang. License conflicts (MIT, Apache 2.0, open core) exist in sources; the company states MIT for the core. Series B investor list is partial (the blog says others participated). The competitor traction and funding then are unknown.
